# Nelux LLM Documentation (llms.txt)

> **Purpose**: Enable AI assistants to understand and correctly use Nelux instantly.
> **Library**: Nelux — High-performance Python video decoding/encoding with GPU acceleration
> **Version**: 0.22.0
> **License**: AGPL-3.0
> **Source**: https://github.com/NevermindNilas/NeLux

---

## Quick Reference

```python
import torch  # MUST be imported before nelux
from nelux import VideoReader, VideoEncoder

# READ: Iterate frames (NVDEC GPU decode)
# Returns HWC tensor: [H, W, C] with native dtype (uint8 for 8-bit, uint16 for 10/12/16-bit)
# C = 3 for color_format="rgb" (default), 4 for "rgba", 1 for "gray"
reader = VideoReader("input.mp4", decode_accelerator="nvdec")
for frame in reader:
    output = model(frame)

# READ: Batch access — returns [B, H, W, C] (always a torch.Tensor)
batch = reader.get_batch([0, 10, 20])
batch = reader[0:100:10]

# READ: Random access — returns [H, W, C]
frame = reader.frame_at(100)       # by index
frame = reader.frame_at(2.5)       # by timestamp (seconds)
frame = reader[100]                # by index
frame = reader[2.5]                # by timestamp
f = reader.get_frame_at(100)       # Frame(data, pts_seconds, duration_seconds)

# WRITE: tensors -> video (CPU or CUDA input; NVENC must be named explicitly)
with VideoEncoder("out.mp4", codec="hevc_nvenc", width=reader.width,
                  height=reader.height, fps=reader.fps) as enc:
    enc.encode_frame(frame)

# TRANSCODE: file -> file without an RGB round trip (ffmpeg-CLI-equivalent output)
import nelux
nelux.transcode("in.mp4", "out.mp4", codec="libx264", options={"crf": "23"})
```

---

## Installation

```bash
pip install nelux
```

Official wheels (v0.9.0+):
- **Windows x64** — CPU + CUDA (NVDEC/NVENC)
- **Linux x86_64** (manylinux_2_28+) — CPU + CUDA
- **macOS arm64** (Apple Silicon, ≥14.0) — CPU + PyTorch MPS (no CUDA on macOS)

**Critical Requirement**: Import `torch` BEFORE `nelux`:
```python
import torch                        # ← FIRST
from nelux import VideoReader       # ← SECOND
```

**FFmpeg is bundled in the wheel** (since 0.17.0) — nothing to install, nothing
to put on `PATH`. Every wheel carries the same pinned build
([TAS-FFMPEG](https://github.com/NevermindNilas/TAS-FFMPEG) 9.0.2), tagged so it
is identifiable at runtime:

```python
nelux.__ffmpeg_version__             # "9.0.2-tas"
```

Anything else means another FFmpeg of the same soname won the load (common on
Windows, where the first DLL of a given name serves the whole process);
`"unknown"` means the extension predates the attribute or — on Windows — no
FFmpeg could be loaded at all.

---

## VideoReader API

### Constructor

```python
VideoReader(
    input_path,                           # str/URL, os.PathLike, bytes/bytearray/memoryview,
                                          #   binary file object, or 1-D CPU uint8 tensor/ndarray
                                          #   (non-path inputs are spooled to a temp file once)
    num_threads: int = 0,                 # 0 = ffmpeg auto-detect
    force_8bit: bool = False,
    backend: Literal["pytorch", "numpy"] = "pytorch",
    decode_accelerator: Literal["cpu", "nvdec"] = "cpu",
    cuda_device_index: int = 0,
    resize: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
    prefetch: bool = False,               # background producer thread
    convert_workers: int | None = None,   # None = min(hw_concurrency, 16); 0 = single-threaded
    color_format: Literal["rgb", "gray", "rgba"] = "rgb",
    resize_filter: Literal[
        "fast_bilinear", "bilinear", "bicubic", "experimental", "neighbor",
        "area", "bicublin", "gauss", "sinc", "lanczos", "spline",
    ] = "bilinear",
    motion_vectors: bool = False,         # opt-in, costs decode time
    stream_index: int | None = None,      # absolute container stream index; None = best video
    *,
    dimension_order: Literal["HWC", "CHW"] = "HWC",  # "CHW" returns CHW/NCHW views (maybe non-contiguous)
    copy_frames: bool = False,            # clone shared CUDA output buffers (to keep/queue frames)
    seek_mode: Literal["exact", "approximate"] = "exact",
    frame_index: FrameIndex | None = None,  # reuse another reader's exact index (same file)
    async_frames: bool = False,           # NVDEC: release decoder surfaces asynchronously
    apply_rotation: bool = True,          # honour container display rotation/flip
)
```

- `seek_mode="exact"` (default): an integer index counts frames in decoded
  presentation order, so VFR, B-frames, open GOPs, repeated/missing PTS and
  timestamp gaps never change which pixels an index selects. The first
  `len()`/`frame_count`, integer random read or non-empty batch lazily scans the
  file with a software decoder (no RGB conversion), also on NVDEC readers;
  construction and sequential iteration do not. Reuse that scan with
  `VideoReader(path, frame_index=other.frame_index)` (same file, same stream; any
  resize/accelerator). `"approximate"` skips the scan and seeks from FPS and
  container counts — faster to start, may differ on VFR/irregular timelines.
- Sequential CUDA output reuses one buffer; pass `copy_frames=True` (or `.clone()`)
  to keep frames. Exact scalar/batch results already own their storage.
- `apply_rotation=True` rotates/flips output per the display matrix; `width`/`height`
  and `properties` keep describing the coded size and report `rotation_degrees`
  and `display_hflip`.

- `backend="pytorch"` → `torch.Tensor`; `backend="numpy"` → `numpy.ndarray` (always CPU, memory-owned copy).
- `decode_accelerator="nvdec"` → frames stay on GPU as CUDA tensors. Auto-falls back to CPU on NVDEC failure.
- `force_8bit=True` → output always `uint8` regardless of source bit depth.
- `color_format="rgb"` (default) → 3-channel HWC `[H, W, 3]`; `"gray"` (aliases `"grayscale"`, `"l"`) → single-channel HWC `[H, W, 1]` luma (libswscale BT.601/709-correct, not a channel average); `"rgba"` → 4-channel HWC `[H, W, 4]` carrying the source alpha plane (ProRes 4444 / 4444 XQ, VP9 or PNG with alpha; alpha is straight, not premultiplied, and a source without alpha yields a fully opaque plane, matching `ffmpeg -pix_fmt rgba`). Both `"gray"` and `"rgba"` are CPU-decode only (batches support them, with fused resize). Read the resulting channel count off `reader.channels`.
- `prefetch=True` → decode on a background thread. Off by default: the producer/consumer queue handoff costs ~2.5x more than the parallelism saves at typical decode speeds.
- `convert_workers=N` → size of the YUV→RGB libswscale convert pool. `None` (default) uses `min(hw_concurrency, 16)` for max throughput; `0` disables the pool (single-threaded convert, matching torchcodec's CPU footprint at the cost of fanout fps); a positive int pins the count.
- `motion_vectors=True` → enable per-frame motion-vector export. Off by default so the decoder skips FFmpeg's motion-vector side-data construction (a real decode-time cost that grows with resolution: measured +6.6% throughput at 720p, +17.1% at 1080p, +18.5% at 4K); `read_frame_with_motion_vectors()` raises while it is off. Never changes decoded pixels.
- `resize=(w, h)` scales frames during decode (CPU: libswscale; NVDEC: cuvid `resize=WxH`). Reported dims and frame shapes reflect the target. `resize_filter` picks the CPU-path scaling kernel (ffmpeg `-sws_flags` names: `bilinear` default, `bicubic`, `lanczos`, `area`, `spline`, …); it governs spatial rescaling only, never color conversion, and is CPU-decode only (NVDEC rejects a non-default value — cuvid uses its own hardware scaler).

### Properties (read-only)

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `width`, `height` | int | Dimensions in pixels |
| `fps` | float | Nominal frames per second (`avg_frame_rate`) |
| `min_fps`, `max_fps` | float | Always equal to `fps` today; for VFR use `properties["is_vfr"]` / `r_frame_rate` |
| `duration` | float | Total duration (seconds) |
| `total_frames` | int | Fast count: `nb_frames`, else an `fps × duration` estimate |
| `frame_count` | int | Exact decoded-frame count in exact mode (built by the lazy index scan, cached); fast header/packet count in approximate mode |
| `metadata` | VideoMetadata | Typed: `width`, `height`, `average_fps`, `duration_seconds`, `num_frames` |
| `frame_index` | FrameIndex | Reusable exact index for this file (pass to another reader) |
| `shape` | tuple | `(frame_count, H, W, channels)` |
| `channels` | int | 3 for `"rgb"`, 4 for `"rgba"`, 1 for `"gray"` |
| `pixel_format` | str | Source pixel format (e.g., `"yuv420p"`) |
| `bit_depth` | int | Bit depth (8, 10, 12, 16) |
| `aspect_ratio` | float | Storage aspect ratio, `width / height` (DAR is `properties["display_aspect_ratio"]`) |
| `codec` | str | Video codec name |
| `has_audio` | bool | Audio track present |
| `file_path` | str | Currently loaded file |
| `properties` | dict | Full ffprobe-equivalent metadata dict (see below) |
| `is_prefetching` | bool | Prefetch thread active |
| `prefetch_buffered` | int | Frames in buffer |
| `prefetch_size` | int | Buffer capacity |
| `frame_type` | str | Type of the last decoded frame: `"I"`, `"P"`, `"B"`, or `""` |
| `ranges`, `current_segment` | list, int | Configured segments; index of the segment the last frame came from (`-1` if none) |

### Metadata (`properties` / `probe`)

`reader.properties` is a superset of the individual accessors, read in-process
from libav (no `ffprobe` subprocess):

```python
p = reader.properties
p["width"], p["height"], p["bit_depth"], p["pixel_format"]
p["avg_frame_rate"], p["r_frame_rate"]      # exact rationals, e.g. "24000/1001"
p["avg_frame_rate_num"], p["avg_frame_rate_den"], p["is_vfr"]
p["nb_frames"], p["total_frames"], p["duration"], p["start_time"]
p["codec"], p["codec_name"], p["codec_long_name"], p["profile"], p["level"]
p["color_primaries"], p["color_transfer"], p["color_space"], p["color_range"]
p["sample_aspect_ratio"], p["display_aspect_ratio"], p["field_order"]
p["bit_rate"], p["format_bit_rate"], p["format_name"], p["nb_streams"]
p["has_audio"], p["audio_codec"], p["audio_sample_rate"], p["audio_channels"]
p["audio_channel_layout"], p["audio_bit_rate"], p["subtitle_codecs"]
p["rotation_degrees"], p["display_hflip"]   # display matrix (applied unless apply_rotation=False)
```

For metadata **without decoding**, use `nelux.probe(path)` — same dict, but it
opens no decoder, allocates no frame buffer and spawns no threads. Results are
cached per file; `nelux.probe_cache_clear()` drops the cache:

```python
import nelux
meta = nelux.probe("video.mp4")      # dict, same keys as VideoReader.properties
```

`total_frames` is fast but falls back to an `fps × duration` estimate when the
container omits `nb_frames` (MKV/WebM/VFR). For an exact count use
`len(reader)` / `reader.frame_count` (exact decoded-frame count from the index
scan, cached), or check `p["nb_frames"] > 0` first to see whether the container
count is authoritative.

### Reading Methods

```python
# Sequential
for frame in reader:                 # [H, W, C]
    ...
frame = reader.read_frame()          # [H, W, C]
reader.reset()                       # back to start (or start of range)

# Random access — does not disturb iterator state
frame = reader.frame_at(100)         # by int index
frame = reader.frame_at(2.5)         # by float timestamp (seconds)
frame = reader[100]                  # by int
frame = reader[2.5]                  # by float

# Batch access — returns [B, H, W, C] torch.Tensor
batch = reader.get_batch([0, 10, 20])
batch = reader.get_batch_range(0, 100, 10)
batch = reader[0:100:10]             # slice
batch = reader[[0, 10, 20]]          # list
batch = reader[range(0, 100, 10)]    # range
batch = reader[torch.tensor([0,5,9])]

len(reader)                          # exact whole-file count; NOT range-aware
                                     #   (set_range/set_ranges do not change it)

# Timed access — Frame / FrameBatch carry data + pts_seconds + duration_seconds
f = reader.get_frame_at(12)                  # Frame
fb = reader.get_frames_at([0, 12, 19])       # FrameBatch (timing: CPU float64 tensors)
f = reader.get_frame_played_at(1.75)         # frame displayed at t=1.75 s (relative to first frame)
fb = reader.get_frames_played_at([0.0, 1.0])
```

### Clip Sampling

```python
import torch, nelux
clips = nelux.samplers.clips_at_indices(reader, [0, 100], num_frames_per_clip=16,
                                        num_indices_between_frames=2, policy="repeat_last")
clips = nelux.samplers.clips_at_random_indices(reader, num_clips=4,
                                               generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(42))
clips = nelux.samplers.clips_at_regular_indices(reader, num_clips=4)
clips = nelux.samplers.clips_at_timestamps(reader, [0.0, 1.0], num_frames_per_clip=8,
                                           seconds_between_frames=0.1)
clips.data            # [clips, frames, H, W, C] (or [..., C, H, W] with dimension_order="CHW")
clips.pts_seconds     # [clips, frames]
```

Each sampler gathers one deduplicated exact batch. Policies: `repeat_last`,
`wrap`, `error`; clip starts must lie inside the video.

`get_batch` deduplicates indices, sorts for sequential decode, and supports
negative indices. `decode_batch(indices)` is the C++ path `get_batch` calls
after normalizing: it bounds-checks, but does not resolve negative indices, so
pass absolute ones.

Slices follow Python container rules: `reader[:0]` is empty, `reader[:-1]` drops
the last frame, `reader[-10:]` is the last ten, `reader[::-1]` is reversed. A
bound past the end raises `IndexError` rather than clamping — but the index list
is materialised before it is validated, so overshoot by a little
(`reader[0:len(reader)+1]`), never by `10**9`. An empty request returns a
`[0, H, W, C]` tensor with the dtype and device a populated batch would have
had.

Batches use the streaming converter's size, colour matrix/range, resize filter
and native uint8/uint16 depth (CPU `rgb`/`gray`/`rgba`, fused resize; NVDEC RGB).
Batch decode always returns a `torch.Tensor`, including under `backend="numpy"`,
and never moves the streaming iterator.

### Motion Vectors

```python
# Opt-in at construction; CPU decode only (NVDEC does not surface side-data).
reader = VideoReader("video.mp4", decode_accelerator="cpu", motion_vectors=True)

frame, vectors = reader.read_frame_with_motion_vectors()   # the ONLY MV reader
reader.frame_type                    # "I" | "P" | "B" | "" for the last frame
```

Each entry in `vectors` is a dict with 10 keys, mirroring FFmpeg's
`AV_FRAME_DATA_MOTION_VECTORS`: `source` (1 = past reference, 2 = future), `w`,
`h` (block size), `src_x`, `src_y` (reference position), `dst_x`, `dst_y` (this
frame's position), `motion_x`, `motion_y` (signed, in `motion_scale` units) and
`motion_scale` (divisor, e.g. 4 for quarter-pel H.264). Divide
`motion_x`/`motion_y` by `motion_scale` for pixel-space displacement.

I-frames — and codecs or decoder builds that do not export the side data —
return an empty list. Calling `read_frame_with_motion_vectors()` without
`motion_vectors=True` raises.

### Frame Ranges

```python
reader.set_range(100, 200)           # frames 100..199 (both int → indices)
reader.set_range(5.0, 10.0)          # both float → seconds
reader.set_range("0:00:05", "0:00:10")  # both str → "H:MM:SS[.ms]" timecode
reader([100, 200])                   # shorthand for set_range(100, 200); returns self
reader.reset()                       # back to start of active range
```

Mixing int and float in `set_range` is an error. Negative indices are supported.

### Multiple Segments (in/out point lists)

```python
reader.set_ranges([(0, 1000), (5000, 6000)])                        # frame indices
reader.set_ranges([(0.0, 7200.0), (10800.0, 14400.0)])              # seconds
reader.set_ranges([("0:00:00", "2:00:00"), ("3:00:00", "4:00:00")])  # timecodes
reader([(0, 1000), (5000, 6000)])    # __call__ shorthand; returns self

for segment, frame in reader.iter_segments():   # (segment_index, frame)
    out = effect_a(frame) if segment == 0 else effect_b(frame)

for frame in reader:                 # unchanged: bare frames, segments back to back
    print(reader.current_segment)    # 0, then 1, ...

reader.ranges                        # [(0, 1000), (5000, 6000)] — frame ends exclusive
reader.clear_ranges()                # back to the whole file
```

Rules: one unit for the whole list (mixing frames and times raises); segments must
be ascending and non-overlapping (touching allowed, e.g. `[(0, 100), (100, 200)]`);
negative frame indices count back from the real decoded EOF (a separate counting
pass). Both units use exclusive outpoints `[start, end)`. Time ranges use actual
presentation timestamps relative to the first decoded frame and reject missing
or decreasing timestamps. Adjacent segments do not repeat a seam frame. Ranges
decode through skipped portions on every backend, so large gaps cost linear
decode time. NVDEC VP9 time ranges additionally use software timestamps because
CUVID can shift timestamps after superframes; output remains on the GPU.

### Prefetch API (Background Buffering)

```python
reader.start_prefetch(buffer_size=16, start_immediately=True)
reader.is_prefetching                # bool
reader.prefetch_buffered             # frames currently buffered
reader.prefetch_size                 # buffer capacity
reader.stop_prefetch()               # stop and free resources
```

Stop prefetch before switching to random access or seeking.

### Decoder Reconfiguration

```python
# Reuse decoder for a different file — 10–50× faster than constructing a new VideoReader
reader.reconfigure("video2.mp4")     # updates all properties, clears range, restarts prefetch
```

### Context Manager / Iteration

```python
with VideoReader("v.mp4") as r:
    for frame in r:
        ...
```

### Encoder Creation

```python
enc = reader.create_encoder("out.mp4")   # matches resolution and fps to source
```

---

## VideoEncoder API

### Constructor

```python
VideoEncoder(
    output_path: str | PathLike | BinaryIO | None = None,  # None = encode into memory
    codec: Optional[str] = None,          # default: container-aware — first available of libx264,
                                          #   libopenh264, h264_mf (Windows) / h264_videotoolbox
                                          #   (macOS) for mp4/mkv/mov/avi/ts; vp9 for webm, gif
                                          #   for gif; image files (.png, .tiff, %05d.bmp, ...)
                                          #   get their extension's encoder. Never auto-NVENC.
    width: Optional[int] = None,          # default: 1920
    height: Optional[int] = None,         # default: 1080
    bit_rate: Optional[int] = None,       # default: 4_000_000 (4 Mbps), unless options set a
                                          #   quality target (crf/qp/cq/global_quality)
    fps: Optional[float] = None,          # default: 30.0; stored as an exact rational
                                          #   (23.976 -> 24000/1001)
    preset: Optional[Union[int, str]] = None,  # int 1..N mapped per codec, or an
                                          #   ffmpeg preset name passed straight through
                                          #   ("medium", "veryfast", "p4", ...)
    cq: Optional[int] = None,             # constant quality (0–51 / 0–63 by codec, lower = better);
                                          #   disables bitrate mode where required
    pixel_format: Optional[str] = None,   # default: "yuv420p"
    options: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,  # extra AVOptions, applied AFTER the built-ins
    resize: bool = False,                 # accept any input size, scale to width x height
    resize_filter: str = "bilinear",      # scaling kernel (ffmpeg -sws_flags names)
    *,
    format: str = "mp4",                  # container for None / file-object destinations
)
```

- GOP length and B-frames are left at each codec's own defaults, as the ffmpeg
  CLI does (since 0.20.0); pin them with `options={"g": "60", "bf": "2"}`.
- `codec="dnxhd"` without `bit_rate`/`profile` encodes DNxHR (HQ/HQX/444 by pixel format).
- `preset` as an int maps through a per-codec table, always **low = faster** (libx264/libx265 `1=ultrafast..9=veryslow`, libsvtav1 `1..9` → SVT `12..4` i.e. fastest to slowest, libaom-av1 → `cpu-used 0..8`, NVENC `1..7` → `p1..p7`); as a str it goes straight to `av_dict_set("preset", value)`, for parity with `ffmpeg -preset <name>`.
- `options` forwards codec-specific AVOption key/value pairs to `avcodec_open2` after the built-in options, so entries here override them: `options={"tune": "film", "x264-params": "ref=3"}`.

Supported `pixel_format` values include `"yuv420p"`, `"nv12"`, `"yuv444p"`, `"p010"`, `"gray"`, `"gray16le"`. Grayscale formats are software-only; NVENC falls back to NV12 with a warning.

dtype decides precision: `uint8` takes the 8-bit path; against a >8-bit output format (`yuv422p10le`, `yuv420p10le`, `p010`, …) a `uint16` tensor is carried through at full 16-bit precision and a float tensor in `[0, 1]` scales to the full 16-bit range. A 4-channel frame's alpha reaches the file only if the output `pixel_format` has an alpha plane (`yuva444p10le` with ProRes 4444 / 4444 XQ); otherwise it is dropped, as `ffmpeg -pix_fmt rgba` does.

CUDA input is converted RGB(A) -> YUV on the GPU — 8- or 16-bit, into
`yuv420p`/`yuvj420p`, `nv12`, `yuv422p`, `yuv444p`, their 10-bit forms and
`p010` — by kernels that write exactly the bytes the CPU (AVX2/libswscale) path
writes, so a CUDA tensor and the same pixels on the CPU give the same bitstream.
NVENC receives the frame without leaving the GPU; software encoders get only
the YUV planes back. CHW views (`chw.permute(1, 2, 0)`) and padded rows need no
`.contiguous()`. Other destinations (gray, RGB, 12-bit, alpha planes) stage
through the CPU. Packed CPU frames into NVENC are uploaded as RGB and converted
by the same kernels. The convert is queued on the current CUDA stream, so later
writes to the tensor on that stream are safe.

- `resize=True` lets `encode_frame` take frames of any spatial size and scales them to `width` × `height` inside the swscale pass the encoder already runs (one fused scale+convert; byte-identical to `ffmpeg -vf scale=WxH:flags=bilinear`). The input size locks to the first frame's shape (a different later size raises), and input must be an explicit HWC layout (`[H,W,3]`/`[H,W,4]`/`[H,W,1]`/`[H,W]` — no flat 1-D buffers). `resize_filter` uses the same scaler names as `VideoReader`'s `resize_filter` and only matters when the sizes differ. A CUDA tensor at a different size takes the CPU staging path (the fused NVENC GPU kernel converts but does not scale); same-size CUDA input keeps the zero-copy GPU path.

Grayscale output (`"gray"`/`"gray16le"`/`"gray16be"`) is a **verbatim, full-range data path**: feed a single-channel `[H,W]`/`[H,W,1]` tensor (`uint8`/`uint16`/`int32`/float; float `[0,1]` scales to the full depth) and values are stored exactly — no range squeeze, up to true 16-bit. A lossless (`ffv1`) round-trip is exact. Ideal for depth maps and masks.

### Methods & Properties

```python
encoder.encode_frame(frame)          # [H, W, 3] RGB, [H, W, 4] RGBA, or [H, W, 1]/[H, W]
                                     #   grayscale tensor (CPU or CUDA)
encoder.close()                      # finalize file
encoder.get_encoded_data()           # output_path=None only: finalizes, returns 1-D CPU uint8
                                     #   tensor (same tensor every call; >16 MiB handed over
                                     #   without a copy; outlives the encoder)
encoder.is_hardware_encoder          # True if NVENC
```

### Destinations: memory and file objects

```python
with VideoEncoder(None, format="mkv", width=640, height=360, fps=30) as enc:
    enc.encode_frame(frame)
data = enc.get_encoded_data()        # torch.uint8 [N]

with open("out.mp4", "wb") as f:     # seekable stream: written while encoding
    with VideoEncoder(f, format="mp4", width=640, height=360) as enc:
        enc.encode_frame(frame)

data = nelux.encode_video(frames, format="mp4", fps=30)   # [N,H,W,C] -> bytes tensor
nelux.encode_video(frames, "out.mp4", fps=30)             # or a path / file object
nelux.encode_video(chw_frames, "out.mp4", dimension_order="CHW")
```

`VideoEncoder`, `encode_video`, `transcode` and `encode_image` all take a path,
a binary file object (written from its current position, left open) or `None`.
Specify `format` when there is no file name. Seekable streams are written as a
file would be; non-seekable ones (pipes, sockets, append mode) receive the
finished container at close.

### Audio / Subtitle Passthrough

Copy (or transcode) audio and subtitle streams from a source file into the
encoded output, with optional `[start, end)` trim in seconds.

```python
encoder.add_passthrough(
    source: str,                     # file to copy audio/subtitle streams from
    audio: bool = True,              # copy audio streams
    subtitles: bool = True,          # copy subtitle streams
    start: float = 0.0,              # trim window start (seconds); rebased to t=0
    end: Optional[float] = None,     # trim window end (seconds); None = to source end
    allow_transcode: bool = True,    # re-encode streams the container can't stream-copy
)
```

- **Must be called before the first `encode_frame`.** Calling it after the first
  frame raises `RuntimeError`.
- **One passthrough source per encoder.** A second `add_passthrough` call raises `RuntimeError`.
- `start`/`end` trim the copied streams and rebase them to `t=0` (no leading
  silence/offset). Match this window to the video frames you push.
- `allow_transcode=True` re-encodes streams whose codec cannot be stream-copied
  into the output container (e.g. AAC→WebM, SubRip→MP4) to the container default
  instead of dropping them. `False` drops un-copyable streams.

```python
reader = VideoReader("input.mp4")
enc = VideoEncoder("clip.mp4", codec="libx264", width=reader.width,
                   height=reader.height, fps=float(reader.fps))
enc.add_passthrough("input.mp4", audio=True, subtitles=True, start=2.0, end=6.0)
# push only the frames for [2.0, 6.0) seconds, then:
enc.close()
```

`nelux.merge_streams(video_source, audio_source, output)` muxes a separate video
file and audio file into one output in-process, stream-copying when the codecs
fit the container.

### Transcoding

```python
nelux.transcode(source, output_path=None, *, format="mp4", start=0.0, end=None,
                audio=True, subtitles=True, allow_transcode=True, **encoder_options)

nelux.transcode("in.mp4", "out.mp4", codec="libx264", preset="veryfast", options={"crf": "23"})
nelux.transcode("in.mp4", "clip.mov", codec="prores_ks", start=2.0, end=6.0)
nelux.transcode("in.mp4", "gpu.mp4", codec="hevc_nvenc")      # decodes on NVDEC
data = nelux.transcode("in.mp4", None, format="mkv", codec="ffv1")
```

Re-encodes video straight from decoded frames (no YUV->RGB->YUV round trip;
one libswscale pass only when the encoder needs another pixel format). Encoder
keywords default to the source's size, exact frame rate, pixel format, colour
tags, chroma location and SAR; display rotation is applied like the CLI's
autorotate; audio/subtitles are copied (timed like `-c:a copy`). Output packets
match `ffmpeg -i in -c:v <codec>` (identical for libx264 at fixed `threads`,
utvideo, ffv1, prores_ks, rawvideo). It does not scale: `width`/`height`
different from the source and `resize=` raise — use `VideoReader` +
`VideoEncoder(resize=True)` instead. Ctrl+C stops it, keeping frames coded so far.

### Context Manager (recommended)

```python
with VideoEncoder("out.mp4", width=1920, height=1080, fps=30) as enc:
    for frame in frames:
        enc.encode_frame(frame)
```

### Create from Reader (matched settings)

```python
with reader.create_encoder("output.mp4") as enc:
    for frame in reader:
        enc.encode_frame(frame)
```

---

## Hardware Acceleration

### NVDEC (GPU Decode)

```python
reader = VideoReader("video.mp4", decode_accelerator="nvdec")
for frame in reader:
    print(frame.device)              # cuda:N — stays on GPU
    result = model(frame)
```

**NVDEC Codecs**: H.264, HEVC (4:4:4 on Ampere+), VP8, VP9, AV1, MPEG-1/2/4, VC1
**NVDEC Formats**: NV12, P010/P016, NV16, P216, YUV444P (8/10/12/16-bit) — all converted to RGB on GPU via custom CUDA kernels.

### NVENC (GPU Encode)

```python
encoder = VideoEncoder("out.mp4", codec="hevc_nvenc")
encoder.is_hardware_encoder          # True
```

**NVENC Codecs**: `h264_nvenc`, `hevc_nvenc`, `av1_nvenc` (GPU-dependent).
NVENC is never chosen automatically — pass `codec=` explicitly. Presets are
`p1`-`p7` (FFmpeg 9 removed the legacy names); `h264_nvenc` defaults to High.

NVENC runs inside torch's CUDA context when that is live on the same device (no
second context, ~222 MiB less VRAM per encoder). Otherwise, the context of the
last closed encoder is cached and reused (`NELUX_NVENC_CONTEXT_CACHE=0`
disables this).

Other hardware encoders in the bundled FFmpeg: QSV and AMF (Windows, Linux),
MediaFoundation (`h264_mf`, Windows) and VideoToolbox (macOS). List them with
`nelux.get_available_encoders()`.

### Zero-Copy GPU Pipeline

NVDEC → CUDA tensor → (model) → NVENC without leaving GPU:

```python
reader = VideoReader("in.mp4", decode_accelerator="nvdec")
with VideoEncoder("out.mp4", codec="hevc_nvenc", width=reader.width,
                  height=reader.height, fps=reader.fps) as enc:
    for frame in reader:
        enc.encode_frame(model(frame))       # RGB -> YUV on the GPU
```

`reader.create_encoder(path)` matches size and fps but uses the default
(software) codec — construct `VideoEncoder` directly to get NVENC.

---

## Images and Audio

```python
image = nelux.decode_image("photo.jpg")                    # [H, W, 3] uint8; bytes/file objects OK
images = nelux.decode_images(["a.jpg", "b.jpg"], device="cuda")  # list (mixed sizes OK); nvJPEG
# decode_image(s) kwargs: device, dimension_order, color_format ("rgb"/"gray"/"rgba"), force_8bit
# CUDA decode: complete RGB/gray JPEGs -> RGB uint8, no EXIF orientation
png = nelux.encode_image(image, format="png")              # 1-D uint8 tensor; 8/16-bit gray/RGB/RGBA
jpg = nelux.encode_image(image, format="jpeg", quality=90, subsampling="420")
                                                           # libjpeg-turbo on CPU (parallel strips),
                                                           #   nvJPEG on CUDA; no alpha
nelux.encode_image(image, "out.png")                       # or write to a path / file object

with nelux.AudioReader("movie.mp4", sample_rate=16000, num_channels=1) as audio:
    s = audio.get_samples_played_in_range(10.0, 20.0)      # AudioSamples
    s.data                                                 # [channels, samples] float32
    everything = audio.get_all_samples()
    audio.metadata                                         # AudioMetadata
```

Audio ranges are exact, sample-aligned slices of the whole decoded stream.
`AudioReader(source, *, stream_index=None, sample_rate=None, num_channels=None, num_threads=1)`.

from nelux import LogLevel, set_log_level

set_log_level(LogLevel.debug)        # trace, debug, info, warn, error, critical, off
```

import nelux

probe_cache_clear()                  # drop cached probe results
suggest_config("clip.mp4")           # (convert_workers, prefetch, note) — report only, never applied
reader.supported_codecs()            # decoders the linked libavcodec provides
```

## Frame Format Reference

| Component | Value |
|---|---|
| Shape (single) | `[H, W, C]` (HWC) — `C` = 3 `"rgb"`, 4 `"rgba"`, 1 `"gray"`; `[C, H, W]` view with `dimension_order="CHW"` |
| Shape (batch) | `[B, H, W, C]` (or `[B, C, H, W]` view), always a `torch.Tensor` |
| dtype (8-bit source) | `uint8` |
| dtype (10/12/16-bit source) | `uint16` |
| dtype (with `force_8bit=True`) | `uint8` |
| Device (CPU decode) | `cpu` |
| Device (NVDEC) | `cuda:N` |
| NumPy backend | always CPU, `numpy.ndarray`, owned memory |

No FP16/FP32, no normalization. Convert explicitly for ML:

```python
frame = reader.read_frame()                         # [H, W, 3] uint8
model_input = frame.permute(2, 0, 1).unsqueeze(0).float() / 255.0   # [1, 3, H, W] float32
```

---

## Best Practices

1. **Import `torch` first.**
2. **Use NVDEC for ML pipelines** — zero CPU/GPU transfer; name an NVENC codec to keep encode on the GPU too.
3. **Prefetch for steady timing** — `reader.start_prefetch(16)` during GPU-bound inference.
4. **Use `reconfigure()` for batch file processing** — 10–50× faster than new instance.
5. **Use `nelux.transcode()` for file -> file re-encodes** — no RGB round trip; use `create_encoder()` when frames pass through your own processing.
6. **Use `get_batch()` / `nelux.samplers` for random-access workloads** — exact indices, smart seek + dedup; share `frame_index` across readers of one file.
7. **Always context-manage the encoder** — otherwise file is not finalized.
8. **Pass `copy_frames=True` to keep sequential NVDEC frames** — the CUDA output buffer is reused.

---

## Common Pitfalls

### Importing nelux before torch
```python
from nelux import VideoReader   # ImportError — torch must be imported first
```

### Expecting CPU tensor from NVDEC
```python
reader = VideoReader("v.mp4", decode_accelerator="nvdec")
frame = next(reader)
frame.numpy()         # Error — frame is on CUDA
frame.cpu().numpy()   # OK
```

### Not closing the encoder
```python
enc = VideoEncoder("out.mp4", ...)
enc.encode_frame(frame)
# file left un-finalized → corrupt

with VideoEncoder("out.mp4", ...) as enc:
    enc.encode_frame(frame)       # properly closed
```

### Mixing int and float in set_range
```python
reader.set_range(100, 10.0)       # Error: int + float
reader.set_range(5.0, 10.0)       # OK (seconds)
reader.set_range(100, 200)        # OK (frame indices)
```

### Out-of-order or overlapping segments
```python
reader.set_ranges([(200, 300), (0, 100)])   # Error: descending
reader.set_ranges([(0, 100), (50, 150)])    # Error: overlapping
reader.set_ranges([(0, 100), (20.0, 30.0)]) # Error: mixed units
reader.set_ranges([(0, 100), (100, 200)])   # OK: touching is allowed
```

---

## Architecture Overview

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      Python API                              │
│  VideoReader (BatchMixin, TemporalMixin)   VideoEncoder      │
│  samplers   transcode / encode_video   images   AudioReader  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                    C++ Backend (_nelux)                      │
│  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐         │
│  │ CPU Decoder │  │CUDA Decoder │  │   Encoder   │         │
│  │ (libswscale)│  │   (NVDEC)   │  │(CPU / NVENC)│         │
│  └──────┬──────┘  └──────┬──────┘  └──────┬──────┘         │
├─────────┼────────────────┼────────────────┼─────────────────┤
│         │     CUDA Kernels (NV12/P010/NV16/YUV444 ↔ RGB)   │
│         │     Color-space conversion on GPU                  │
├─────────┼────────────────┼────────────────┼─────────────────┤
│         └────────────────┼────────────────┘                  │
│                        FFmpeg                                │
│         Format/codec handling, muxing/demuxing               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Color spaces supported: BT.709, BT.601/SMPTE170M, BT.2020, SMPTE 240M, FCC — both limited (TV: 16–235) and full range (PC: 0–255).

---

## Supported Codecs

### Decode
| Codec | CPU | NVDEC |
|---|---|---|
| H.264/AVC | ✓ | ✓ |
| H.265/HEVC | ✓ | ✓ |
| VP8 | ✓ | ✓ |
| VP9 | ✓ | ✓ |
| AV1 | ✓ | ✓ |
| MPEG-1/2/4 | ✓ | ✓ |
| VC1 | ✓ | ✓ |
| ProRes, DNxHD/HR, DV | ✓ | ✗ |

### Encode
| Codec | Software | NVENC | Other hardware |
|---|---|---|---|
| H.264 | libx264 | h264_nvenc | h264_qsv, h264_amf, h264_mf, h264_videotoolbox |
| H.265 | libx265 | hevc_nvenc | hevc_qsv, hevc_amf, hevc_mf, hevc_videotoolbox |
| AV1 | libsvtav1, libaom-av1 | av1_nvenc | av1_qsv, av1_amf |
| VP8 / VP9 | libvpx, libvpx-vp9 | — | — |
| Intermediate / lossless | prores_ks, prores_aw, dnxhd (DNxHR), ffv1, utvideo, huffyuv/ffvhuff, rawvideo, … | — | — |
| Images | png, mjpeg, tiff, libwebp, jpeg2000, dpx, exr, bmp, sgi, targa, … | — | — |

Exact availability depends on platform and GPU; `nelux.get_available_encoders()`
is authoritative. Still-image codecs without libavcodec threading (dpx, sgi,
targa, bmp, pnm, …) and libwebp code several frames at once, byte-identically.

### Containers
Anything libavformat muxes/demuxes: MP4, MKV, MOV, WebM, AVI, MPEG-TS
(concatenated TS decodes across splices), GIF, image sequences (`%05d.png`),
Y4M, raw elementary streams. `format=` names the container for memory/file-object
output (default: MP4).

---

## Complete Example: ML Video Processing

```python
import torch
from nelux import VideoReader, VideoEncoder

def process_video(input_path, output_path, model):
    gpu = torch.cuda.is_available()
    reader = VideoReader(input_path, decode_accelerator="nvdec" if gpu else "cpu")
    reader.start_prefetch(buffer_size=16)

    with VideoEncoder(output_path, codec="hevc_nvenc" if gpu else None,
                      width=reader.width, height=reader.height, fps=reader.fps) as encoder:
        encoder.add_passthrough(input_path)                 # keep audio/subtitles
        for frame in reader:                                # [H, W, 3] on GPU (NVDEC)
            x = frame.permute(2, 0, 1).unsqueeze(0).float() / 255.0
            y = model(x)
            out = (y.squeeze(0).permute(1, 2, 0) * 255).to(torch.uint8)
            encoder.encode_frame(out)

    reader.stop_prefetch()
    print(f"Processed {len(reader)} frames")
```

---

## Version History Highlights

- **0.22.0** (2026-11-01): PyTorch 2.15.0 / torchvision 0.29.2 (cu132), `215torch` ABI-tagged wheels that refuse to import under another torch minor (stay on 0.21.x for PyTorch 2.14); Python 3.15 wheels on Windows, Linux and macOS alongside 3.13 and 3.14.
- **0.21.0** (2026-10-28): Encoder overhaul — byte-exact AVX2 and CUDA RGB->YUV converters (CPU and CUDA input give identical bitstreams), frame-parallel encoding for 25 intra codecs (sgi 7.4x, libwebp 11x the ffmpeg CLI), CPU frames into NVENC converted on the GPU at every size, NVENC sharing torch's CUDA context, float/uint16/CHW input without torch ops, `nelux.transcode()` (CLI-equivalent autorotate, pixel format, colour tags and audio sync), file-object and zero-copy memory output, many broken encoder defaults fixed, and the 0.20.0 race where a CUDA frame rewritten after `encode_frame` (or an NVDEC frame fed straight in) was encoded wrong.
- **0.20.0** (2026-10-17): `VideoEncoder` leaves GOP length and B-frames at each codec's own defaults like the ffmpeg CLI (was forced g=60/bf=2: -2.6 dB on libx264, B-frames in NVENC p1); pin with `options={"g", "bf"}`. FFmpeg 9.0.2 (soname 63), PyTorch 2.14.1, `merge_streams()`, `subtitle_codecs`, in-memory still-image decode, faster `AudioReader`, MOV Opus/Vorbis passthrough transcodes to AAC, NVDEC exact-read hang and limited-range high-bit-depth fixes.
- **0.19.0** (2026-09-14): PyTorch 2.14.0 / torchvision 0.29.0, `214torch` ABI-tagged wheels; exact decoded-frame range counting, exclusive first-frame-relative time bounds, VP9 superframe fixes, explicit integer-versus-time `frame_at` dispatch, and corpus-driven installed-wheel CI gates. Large range gaps now decode linearly; NVDEC VP9 time cuts add CPU timing decode work.
- **0.18.0** (2026-08-12): **Encoder-side resize** — `VideoEncoder(..., resize=True, resize_filter=...)` accepts input frames of any size and scales them to `width`×`height` inside the encoder's existing swscale pass (fused scale+convert, byte-identical to `ffmpeg -vf scale=WxH:flags=bilinear`, verified across every bundled software encoder family plus NVENC/QSV). Input size locks to the first frame; RGBA alpha, deep uint16/float and the verbatim gray data path all resample correctly (gray at output bit depth). Also fixes RGB-destination scaling colour-matrix skew (unreachable pre-resize) and ships the container-aware default codec + `av_guess_format` container inference fixes from the unreleased train.
- **0.17.0** (2026-07-25): **Critical CUDA fix** — the architecture guard sat after `enable_language(CUDA)`, so it was dead code and every wheel shipped a single architecture; PTX only JITs forward, so every older GPU failed every kernel launch with `cudaErrorNoKernelImageForDevice` and returned fully black frames. Device code is now built for `75;80;86;89;90` (+`60;70` on CUDA <13, +`100;120` on CUDA >=12.8), and CUDA launches are error-checked instead of silently no-opping. Published CUDA 13 wheels need compute capability 7.5+. Also fixes `set_range(start, end)` returning frames at `keyframe + start` on NVDEC (#57), a process abort on `set_range(start_time > 0)` with CPU frame threading (#60), and CPU batch decode converting YUV→RGB with BT.601 regardless of the stream's `color_space` (#58, up to 40/255 error on bt709). `decode_batch` is **3-8x faster** (cached scaler + row `memcpy` + frame threading, byte-exact); `NELUX_ENABLE_AVX2` now defaults OFF (measured no-op, and it hard-required AVX2); encoder convert workers capped at 4 (+2.0% on 720p mpeg4, byte-identical output, ~74 MB less pool RAM at 4K).
- **0.16.0** (2026-07-19): Motion-vector export is now opt-in via `VideoReader(motion_vectors=True)`. Off by default, the CPU decoder skips libavcodec's per-frame motion-vector side-data construction, raising decode throughput (720p +6.6%, 1080p +17.1%, 4K +18.5%, byte-identical output). BREAKING: the motion-vector read API is consolidated to `read_frame_with_motion_vectors()`; `read_motion_vectors()` and the `motion_vectors` / `motion_vectors_array` properties are removed (`frame_type` stays). Also fixes RGB→P210 10-bit 4:2:2 encode scaling (`<<6`→`<<8`) and guards NVENC `b_ref_mode` behind `max_b_frames > 0`.
- **0.15.1** (2026-07-19): Added `nelux.probe(path)`, a decode-free metadata reader returning the same dict as `VideoReader.properties`. It opens no decoder, allocates no resolution-sized frame tensor, and spawns no threads, so it strips nelux's per-open decode setup and avoids the process spawn an external `ffprobe` call pays: ~37x faster than an `ffprobe` subprocess at 360p and ~2.2x at 4K, output verified identical to `.properties` across the 135-clip corpus. Metadata extraction was refactored into a shared `AVCodecParameters`-only path used by both the live decoder and `probe()`.
- **0.15.0** (2026-07-19): `VideoReader.properties` now exposes a full ffprobe-equivalent metadata set read in-process from libav (no `ffprobe` subprocess, no new dependency): canonical `codec_name`, `codec_long_name`, `profile`/`level`, exact `r_frame_rate`/`avg_frame_rate` rationals (+ `_num`/`_den`) with `is_vfr`, raw `nb_frames`, `color_primaries`/`color_transfer`/`color_space`/`color_range`, `sample_aspect_ratio`/`display_aspect_ratio`, `bit_rate`/`format_bit_rate`, `start_time`, `field_order`, `format_name`/`format_long_name`, `nb_streams`, and first-audio-stream details. Verified field-for-field against ffprobe on a 135-clip corpus and measured ~12–14× faster than an ffprobe call. `get_frame_count()`/`len()` now return an exact demux-counted total (matching `ffprobe -count_packets`) when the container omits `nb_frames`, instead of an `fps × duration` estimate; `total_frames` stays the fast estimate.
- **0.14.3** (2026-07-10): Fixed NVDEC batched decode returning the wrong frame — `get_batch()` (and slice/list indexing) with `decode_accelerator="nvdec"` intermittently returned a neighbouring or torn frame due to a cross-context CUDA surface race; `frame_at` had the same ±1 flicker. The hw decoder now shares PyTorch's CUDA context and synchronizes cuvid's producer stream before conversion, so NVDEC `get_batch`/`frame_at`/iteration are bit-exact and deterministic. CPU decode was unaffected.
- **0.14.2** (2026-07-10): `VideoReader(..., resize_filter=...)` selects the libswscale scaling kernel for the decoder-side `resize` (ffmpeg `-sws_flags` names; CPU decode only, rejected with `decode_accelerator="nvdec"`). Build dependency bumped to PyTorch 2.13.0 / torchvision 0.28.0 (Windows + Linux on the CUDA 13.2 `cu132` wheel index); wheels are ABI-tagged `213torch` and refuse to import under a different PyTorch minor.
- **0.12.2** (2026-05-28): Fixed Windows CUDA wheels failing to import (`ImportError: DLL load failed ... WinError 1114`) — the release `delvewheel` repair step now excludes `c10_cuda.dll` so it is no longer double-vendored alongside torch's copy. No API or runtime behavior change.
- **0.12.1** (2026-05-28): Build dependency bumped to PyTorch 2.12.0 / torchvision 0.27.0 (Windows + Linux build against the CUDA 13.2 `cu132` wheel index). Runtime `torch` stays unpinned — wheels exclude torch and use the installed copy.
- **0.12.0** (2026-05-27): `VideoEncoder.add_passthrough(source, audio, subtitles, start, end, allow_transcode)` — copy/transcode audio + subtitle streams from a source into the output with `[start, end)` trim + rebase; one source per encoder, must precede first `encode_frame`. Async fan-out encode pipeline (RGB→YUV convert workers + seq-keyed reorder). `encode_frame` validates input size up front (`ValueError` on mismatch).
- **0.11.0** (2026-05-16): `libyuv` dependency removed — pure libswscale CPU pipeline (`SWS_BILINEAR`, byte-identical to `ffmpeg -vf format=rgb24`); faster on every YUV path.
- **0.9.1** (2026-04-22): Suppressed libx264/libx265/libsvtav1 banner and per-frame info noise from encoder output (av_log level + `x265-params=log-level=none` + fd-2 redirect around SVT-AV1 init/teardown).
- **0.9.0** (2026-04-18): Official Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64 wheels; per-platform FFmpeg resolution; LTO/AVX2 extended to CUDA compilation; `NELUX_ENABLE_CUDA_FAST_MATH` option; real post-install smoke test.
- **0.8.10**: PyTorch 2.11.0 / TorchVision 0.26.0 baseline.
- **0.8.9**: Fixed NumPy backend memory-aliasing bug (arrays now own their memory); Windows wheels bundle FFmpeg + libyuv + fmt + spdlog + turbojpeg DLLs; `diagnose_runtime_dlls()` helper.
- **0.8.8**: Full NVENC hardware-encoding support; improved color accuracy.
- **0.8.7**: `import torch` before `nelux` became mandatory; HWC uint8/uint16 standardized (no BCHW, no FP16/FP32).
- **0.8.6**: Zero-copy GPU encoding (CUDA ↔ NVENC); custom CUDA conversion kernels; 1080p NVENC ≈ 410 FPS.

---

## Requirements

- Python **3.13+** (`requires-python = ">=3.13"`)
- PyTorch **2.15.x** — each wheel is built against one torch minor, is
  build-tagged (`215torch`) and raises `ImportError` under a different minor.
  The matching CUDA torch wheel supplies the CUDA runtime the NVDEC path needs.
- CUDA **13.x** for the published NVDEC/NVENC wheels; GPU compute capability
  7.5+ (Turing or newer). Pre-Turing NVDEC cards need a source build against
  CUDA 12.x. CPU-only builds drop this entirely.
- FFmpeg — **bundled in the wheel**, nothing to install
- Windows 10/11, Linux (manylinux_2_28+), or macOS 14.0+ (arm64)
